deploymentEvidence.note: Current primary API explicitly links ForgeYields WBTC to Ethereum token gateway; official own financial share and epoch ledger product distinct from downstream Veda strategy custody.

lifecycleEvidence.note: Current own product docs offer fyUSDC/fyETH/fyWBTC, automatic allocation and asynchronous redemption; no shutdown claim is inferred from idle/paused sibling gateway.
Selected WBTC gateway observed not paused, not stale and not preparing/depreciated. Static point-in-time only.

configurationObservations.note: No sibling ETH/USDC active capability is proposed. Their paused/stale result is deployment-specific, not proof entire project is retired.

selectedFunctions.label: ForgeYields claimRedeem financial call
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory. All selected calls are nonpayable and require zero native value.

Only Ethereum fyWBTC TokenGateway 0xedca8230366b9eaff06becdd1d261577836aa507 is admitted. Current transparent implementation 0xf1d326d806fa5d0d1f3747505397553cd31b191a and proxy each have Sourcify exact_match runtime and creation records. EIP-1967 slot read at block 26261586 resolves the same implementation. Ownership and proxy admin remain mutable.

ForgeYields owns the gateway share accounting, buffer, epoch redemption ledger and NFT request flow; it is not only a curator label on an admitted Veda vault. The strategy layer uses Veda BoringVault infrastructure and the global controller is on unsupported Starknet. No controller, bridging, relayer reporting, arbitrary strategy management, transfer, approval, permit or signing authority is admitted.

At the recorded block fyWBTC isPaused, isStale, depreciated and prepareToDepreciate were false. ETH and USDC sibling gateways were paused/stale and are not admitted. These are point-in-time observations, not continued availability guarantees; epoch freshness, mutable caps and owner pause control can reject calls.

Underlying is Ethereum WBTC 0x2260fac5e5542a773aa44fbcfedf7c193bc2c599; both underlying amounts and fyWBTC shares use 8 decimals. PPS has 1e18 scale. Deposit floors shares; mint rounds required assets up; inputs are pulled exclusively from msg.sender. receiver receives minted shares. There is no caller minimum-shares/maximum-assets parameter. Referral code is only Deposit event attribution, not an executable payload or authority grant.

requestRedeem burns owner shares net of a floor-rounded redeem fee transferred as shares to feesRecipient. If caller differs from owner it spends a preexisting allowance; this catalog grants no allowance. Fee observed 0.0005 of shares; owner can change it up to 0.001. Asset conversion floors at current PPS, consumes epoch withdrawal capacity, and creates a redeem NFT for receiver. No caller minimum payout or deadline exists.

Source takes precedence over generic documentation: request NFT stores epoch and nominal asset value (field named shares), not original fyWBTC share units. claimRedeem is permissionless, burns the request NFT and pays its CURRENT owner, not an immutable original receiver. Transferring the NFT transfers the claim; no NFT transfer or authorization capability is admitted.

Claims require an epoch already handled by controller reporting and sufficient locked WBTC. Payout floors nominal request value times remaining epoch assets divided by remaining nominal epoch value; loss and rounding are possible. State and locked balance reduce before transfer. No epoch settlement/report/bridge capability or claim deadline is promised. Dependency interfaces are retained; independent runtime/backing attestations for every controller, bridge, NFT or downstream strategy are not asserted.

sourceSnapshots.content: > For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://forge-labs.gitbook.io/forge-docs/llms.txt). Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://forge-labs.gitbook.io/forge-docs/basics/readme.md). # Introduction **Higher yields demand higher craft.** ForgeYields is a cross-chain yield aggregator for the frontier — strategies blue-chip aggregators won't touch, underwritten like structured credit. ## Why ForgeYields Yield aggregators give you safe-list returns. Anonymous farms ask you to take their word for it. ForgeYields gives you the frontier — with the discipline of structured credit. Tracking dozens of protocols. Rebalancing across chains as incentives shift. Underwriting every position before deposit. # fyTokens

**fyTokens are the ERC-4626 yield-bearing tokens you receive when you deposit into a ForgeYields vault.** One fyToken represents a proportional share of a vault's underlying assets — and of every Hallmark-underwritten strategy the vault is currently deployed across.

ForgeYields currently offers three vault tokens, each directional in its underlying: **fyUSDC** (USDC), **fyETH** (ETH), **fyWBTC** (WBTC). Each vault's composition — strategies, weights, current GRS per position — is published in real time and changes as the allocator rebalances. Every strategy in the mix must have a current Hallmark score and an APPROVED verdict under the [ForgeYields Allocator Policy](/forge-docs/hallmark/allocator-policy.md) before the allocator can deploy to it.

## What they do

* **Auto-compound.** Rewards accrue to the share price. The token count stays the same; the value of each token grows.
* **Liquid.** No lockup. Hold, transfer, or trade fyTokens anytime — they're standard ERC-4626 receipts.
* **Composable.** Use as collateral in lending markets, integrate into other protocols, bridge across L2s. Your yield position is a usable asset, not a frozen deposit.
* **Cross-chain.** Deposit from any supported chain; the vault settles on Ethereum. You receive fyTokens on the chain you deposited from.
* **Asynchronous redemption.** Withdraw via a request-then-claim flow. Funds stay earning until the next clearing cycle (typically minutes to hours, depending on liquidity). See [Redeem](/forge-docs/user-guide/redeem.md) for the user flow.

## What backs them

Every fyToken's value depends on the strategies the underlying vault is allocated to. Those strategies are:

* Scored by [Hallmark](/forge-docs/hallmark/overview.md) and APPROVED under the [Allocator Policy](/forge-docs/hallmark/allocator-policy.md)
* Continuously monitored — a score deterioration that flips the Policy verdict to EXCLUDED triggers exit, not optimization
* Fully transparent — every score, every methodology version, every cascade dependency is [publicly verifiable](/forge-docs/hallmark/transparency.md)

You're not holding an IOU against an unknown set of farms. You're holding a share in a vault whose entire allocation universe is published and audited.

## Why this matters

Most yield aggregators give you a token that grows in value with no insight into what's behind it. fyTokens come with a published risk score for every strategy that contributes to the share price — and an immediate alert if that score degrades. This is the institutional bar applied to retail-accessible vaults.

Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://forge-labs.gitbook.io/forge-docs/how-it-works/overall.md). # Architecture Understand ForgeYields cross-chain architecture ### Architecture Breakdown #### **1. User Interface Layer (Token Gateways on Each Chain)** Users interact with ForgeYields through Token Gateways deployed on each supported chain (Starknet, Ethereum, Scroll). These gateways: * Receive **deposit** and **redeem** requests * Perform **local netting** * Handle cross-chain transfers through canonical bridges * Forward asset flows and reports to the global Controller This layer abstracts all multi-chain complexity. Users only interact on their chain of choice while the system handles settlement across others. *** #### **2. Coordination Layer (Controller on Starknet)** The Controller contract on Starknet is the global coordination hub. It: * Receives **Token Gateway Reports** (deposit totals, redemption totals) * Receives **Vault Reports** (executed trades, AUM updates) * Calculates global AUM and rollup-specific deltas * Sends back the **Controller Report** to all Token Gateways * Triggers settlement across chains This layer also uses an **Oracle Role** that submits off-chain prices, AUM snapshots, and cross-chain state needed to maintain the global epoch logic. The Controller is intentionally isolated and minimalist, improving auditability and reducing attack surface. *** #### **3. Underwriting Layer (**[**Hallmark**](/forge-docs/hallmark/overview.md) **+** [**Allocator Policy**](/forge-docs/hallmark/allocator-policy.md)**)** Before a strategy can enter the Strategist's allow-list, it is scored by Hallmark — the published methodology that scores chain, protocol, asset, and strategy (four layers, including curator/atomist trust for wrapper vaults) on a 1–10 scale. Hallmark publishes descriptive scores and labels only; the ForgeYields [Allocator Policy](/forge-docs/hallmark/allocator-policy.md) derives the verdicts (APPROVED / EXCLUDED), concentration caps, and exit rules from those scores. * Every score is published and versioned ([forge-hallmark](https://github.com/ForgeYields/forge-hallmark)) * Scores cascade: an L1 protocol rescore triggers re-evaluation of every L3 strategy in its dependency tree * The allocator refuses any strategy without a current score or without an APPROVED verdict under the Allocator Policy * No "manual override" path exists — the validators are enforced in the allocator pipeline This is the gate between "we could deploy here" and "we will deploy here." *** #### **4. Strategy Execution Layer (Manager + Vault on Ethereum)** This layer is where eligible capital is allocated and yield is generated. **Vault (Ethereum, via** [**Veda Labs BoringVault**](https://docs.veda.tech)**):** * Receives assets bridged from Token Gateways * Deposits into Policy-approved strategies across Aave, Morpho, Curve, Pendle, Ipor Fusion, MetaMorpho, Convex, Yearn V3, and others * Executes trades and rebalances liquidity * Sends Vault Reports back to the Controller **Manager (Ethereum):** * Enforces the **Merkle-based allowed calls** (set off-chain by the Strategist, gated by the Allocator Policy's APPROVED set) * Ensures only vetted integrations and methods can be executed * Acts as the "instruction layer" for strategy changes **Strategist (Off-chain engine):** * Computes target allocations across the Policy-approved set — targets are approved by the risk committee before execution * Allowed actions defined via Merkle roots * Sends instructions through the Manager to perform swaps, deposits, and reallocations *** #### **5. Mailboxes (Hyperlane) Across Chains** At the top of each layer, Mailboxes (Starknet, Ethereum, Scroll) handle: * Cross-chain messaging * Report synchronization * Controlled dispatch between Token Gateways, Controller, and Vault This enables a **fully distributed yet unified global state** across all chains. *** ### Summary This architecture separates ForgeYields into four clean layers: * **User Interface Layer** → local deposit/redeem, chain abstraction * **Coordination Layer** → global AUM, epochs, cross-chain state * **Underwriting Layer (Hallmark + Allocator Policy)** → risk scoring, verdicts and caps, cascade integrity * **Strategy Execution Layer** → deployment to eligible strategies, allowed calls Each component has a minimal, clearly defined responsibility, ensuring security, scalability, and fast strategy upgrades.
